details.whyNow: Success in one domain attracts interest from others. But more importantly, testing across multiple coordination problems (democratic systems, peer review, resource allocation, trust networks, etc.) lets us validate whether our simulation approach actually predicts real-world outcomes. If mechanisms that perform well in our simulations consistently succeed in real deployment, we've created genuine predictive infrastructure. This confidence is essential before attempting generative design.
details.whatWereDoing: As Phase 2 demonstrates value, researchers working on different coordination failures want to test their proposals. We expand infrastructure to handle new domains while rigorously measuring whether our simulation results predict real-world performance. This is the validation phase - we're not just testing policies, we're testing whether our testing works. We accumulate a dataset of "what works under what conditions" across multiple contexts. Real-world pilots expand from single communities to multiple deployments across different cultural and institutional contexts.
details.buildingConfidence: The key output isn't just "we tested 50 policies" but "we can predict with X% confidence which mechanisms will work in which contexts." We develop metrics for simulation validity, understand where our models succeed and fail, and identify the boundaries of reliable prediction. During this phase, we may discover our foundational frameworks missed important dynamics - the backward loop to Phase 1 is most likely here. By the end, we have validated infrastructure, a track record of successful predictions, multiple domains covered, and enough data to begin systematic mechanism generation.
